skill.name: backtest-expert
skill.description: Expert guidance for systematic backtesting of trading strategies. Use when developing, testing, stress-testing, or validating quantitative trading strategies. Covers "beating ideas to death" methodology, parameter robustness testing, slippage modeling, bias prevention, and interpreting backtest results. Applicable when user asks about backtesting, strategy validation, robustness testing, avoiding overfitting, or systematic trading development.
skill.summary: Evaluate trading strategies with structured scoring, stress tests, bias checks, and realistic execution assumptions.
skill.author: tradermonty

content.value_statement: Backtest results can hide overfitting, weak samples, and unrealistic execution assumptions. This skill applies structured scoring, stress tests, and bias checks.
actual_capabilities: Scores backtests across sample size, expectancy, risk management, robustness, and execution realism.
Calculates profit factor and expected return per trade from supplied summary metrics.
Flags small samples, excessive drawdowns, negative expectancy, over-optimization, and missing slippage tests.
Guides parameter sensitivity, walk-forward, market regime, and execution friction testing.
Produces local Markdown and structured evaluation reports with Deploy, Refine, or Abandon verdicts.
Provides checklists for detecting survivorship, look-ahead, hindsight, and sample selection biases.
limitations: It evaluates user-provided summary metrics and does not run a market-data backtest.
Its scoring thresholds are general heuristics, not guarantees of future performance.
It does not retrieve prices, broker costs, or external datasets.
It does not replace independent statistical review, risk controls, or financial advice.

use_cases.title: Screen a New Strategy
use_cases.description: Review early backtest metrics and identify the highest-priority validation gaps before further development.

use_cases.title: Challenge Research Results
use_cases.description: Apply bias checks, parameter stress tests, and walk-forward criteria during a formal research review.

use_cases.title: Teach Robust Validation
use_cases.description: Demonstrate why sample size, execution friction, market regimes, and out-of-sample testing affect confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this backtest: [trades], [win rate], [average win], [average loss], [drawdown], [years], [parameters], and [slippage tested]. Explain the verdict simply.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first review with complete summary metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Stress Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a stress test plan for this strategy: [rules]. Cover parameter ranges, slippage, commissions, fill quality, sample size, and market regimes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before accepting initial backtest results.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Backtest
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these failed backtest results: [results]. Identify breaking points, likely biases, weak assumptions, and the next tests that could reject or refine the hypothesis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when results deteriorate under validation.

prompt_templates.title: Conduct an Adversarial Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this strategy and evidence: [strategy], [metrics], [periods], [cost assumptions], [parameter tests], and [out-of-sample results]. Produce a prioritized robustness assessment and deployment conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced review before live implementation.

output_examples.input: Evaluate 150 trades, 62 percent wins, 1.8 percent average win, 1.2 percent average loss, 15 percent drawdown, eight years, three parameters, with slippage tested.
output_examples.output: Deploy, 81 out of 100. The sample, expectancy, drawdown, test duration, parameter count, and execution assumptions support further consideration. Independent validation remains necessary.

output_examples.input: Review 24 trades over two years with eight parameters and no slippage test.
output: The sample is below the minimum threshold.
The test period may omit important market regimes.
Eight parameters indicate substantial overfitting risk.
Execution costs have not been validated.

output_examples.input: Explain why a profitable strategy fails after realistic trading costs.
output_examples.output: The reported edge is smaller than expected slippage and commissions. Test conservative fills and nearby parameters before deciding whether the hypothesis remains viable.

best_practices: Define entry, exit, sizing, filters, and the trading universe before testing.
Use multiple market regimes, out-of-sample periods, and conservative execution costs.
Prefer broad performance plateaus over isolated optimal parameter values.
anti_patterns: Do not select only successful instruments, periods, or examples.
Do not optimize many parameters and report only the best configuration.
Do not treat a high score or historical return as proof of future performance.

faq.question: Does this skill run a complete backtest?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates supplied summary metrics and provides a methodology for testing a strategy.

faq.question: Does it need market data or API keys?
faq.answer: No. The evaluator uses local inputs and Python standard-library features.

faq.question: What reports does the script create?
faq.answer: It creates timestamped Markdown and structured evaluation files in the selected output directory.

faq.question: What does a Deploy verdict mean?
faq.answer: It means the supplied metrics meet the heuristic score threshold. It does not guarantee profitability or readiness for live capital.

faq.question: Can it detect overfitting?
faq.answer: It flags high parameter counts and guides sensitivity and out-of-sample tests. Definitive detection requires deeper statistical analysis.

faq.question: Is this financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It is a research framework and evaluation tool. Users remain responsible for investment decisions and risk management.
